_comment: Operator-supplied photography — photographs of the ACTUAL vendor, given to us by them.
manifest.json is Wikimedia Commons only and will refuse anything else, which is correct: it
cannot verify a licence it cannot look up. This file is the other route. The trade is that
nothing here can be verified automatically, so provenance is recorded by hand instead and
fetch.py refuses to write an entry that does not carry it.
2. Add an entry below with the same <key>
<key> is the media key the dataset already uses, e.g. jm-mystic-1 — adding it here overrides
whatever manifest.json says for that key.
`rightsHolder` and `permission` are both required and both end up in the app's credit line.
Write what is actually true in `permission`: 'Email from Marketing, 12 Sep 2026' is useful a

_example-jm-mystic-1.subject: The bobsled at Mystic Mountain, Ocho Rios, Jamaica
_example-jm-mystic-1.permission: REPLACE ME — e.g. 'Media kit supplied by <name>, <date>' or 'Written permission, email <date>'
